label: map_1
name: Experimenting Causal Program Library
mech: The system keeps a growing library of small probabilistic programs, each encoding a candidate causal mechanism (e.g., "pressure causes leak if seal is worn"). When several programs explain the observations equally well, it computes which intervention (real action, simulator query or tool call) would best tell them apart, runs it, and reweights or deletes programs based on the result. New programs are synthesized by recombining fragments of programs that survived, so the library compresses over time.
value: It can discover and reliably use real cause-and-effect structure, including in situations that never appeared in its data.

label: map_1
name: Self-Revising Provenance Belief Ledger
mech: Every assertion the system adopts becomes a node in a persistent graph that stores its source, confidence and the nodes it was derived from. On each inference step a constraint checker scans for contradictions. Conflicts are resolved by retracting the least-supported justification, and the retraction automatically propagates to all dependent conclusions (truth maintenance). Generation is restricted to drawing on the active ledger and has to cite node IDs.
value: It enables lifelong learning without catastrophic forgetting, with traceable reasoning and instant correction of any fact and everything derived from it.

label: map_1
name: Information-Priced Compute Market
mech: Many heterogeneous modules (search, simulation, symbolic solvers, small neural nets) bid for slices of a shared compute budget. A bid is priced by the expected reduction in task uncertainty, and the payout is the realized reduction. Modules that bid well gain budget and get copied with mutations, while chronically bad bidders are retired. The architecture is therefore an evolving economy rather than a fixed graph.
value: It makes possible adaptive, open-ended allocation of reasoning effort and self-directed architectural growth after deployment.

label: map_2
name: Audited Sleep Consolidation
mech: Surprising experiences go verbatim into a fast episodic buffer. During offline phases the system replays them to propose weight deltas inside a sandboxed copy of its slow network. Each delta is accepted only if a self-maintained regression suite of past skills shows no loss, and rejected deltas are stored as interference records that shape later proposals.
value: It enables continual lifelong learning after deployment without catastrophic forgetting.

label: map_2
name: Evolving Executable World Simulators
mech: The system maintains a population of small probabilistic programs, each a candidate simulator of some part of the environment. Queries are answered by running or intervening on the best-scoring simulators. Prediction errors drive program-synthesis mutations, and simulators are selected by how well they compress observations and predict accurately.
value: It gives explicit causal and counterfactual reasoning and lets the system discover new models that can be inspected.

label: map_2
name: Verified Competence Cartography
mech: An embedding-indexed map stores the system's ground-truth-verified error statistics for each region of problem space, updated whenever an outcome is checked. Before answering, the system looks up the query's region. It then answers, abstains, asks for information, or routes the region to the learning loop, depending on the measured reliability and the cost of being wrong.
value: It gives reliable self-knowledge of where the system is competent, so it can abstain and direct its own learning based on its actual track record.

label: map_3
name: Surprise-Gated Synaptic Patch Memory
mech: When prediction error on an input crosses a learned threshold, the system writes a small key-value module next to the frozen core. The key is the context embedding and the value is a low-rank change to the core's weights. Those changes take effect only when a later context is similar to that key. During an offline phase, the system replays old episodes against the patches. It merges patches that do the same thing and deletes ones that conflict, using how often they agree as the score. Each patch keeps a count of how often it was used and how often it was confirmed, and patches that stop earning their place are removed.
value: The system could learn permanently from a single experience without forgetting what it already knows or needing retraining.

label: map_3
name: Falsifiable Causal World-Graph
mech: Perception updates a running graph of objects, their attributes and typed causal links. Each link carries a probability and a count of how many times its predictions came true. Before each step the system simulates what it expects to observe, then compares that with what it actually observes. When they differ, it traces the error back through the graph to the links most to blame and revises them: it adds hidden variables, splits links or reverses their direction. It can also run interventions inside the graph to test competing explanations before acting.
value: The system could know when its beliefs are wrong, reason about counterfactuals, and keep a consistent, inspectable model of the world over long periods.

label: map_3
name: Verifier-Halted Constraint Relaxation
mech: A query is turned into a set of variables, which are partial answers and sub-goals, plus constraints between them that are learned or extracted from the query. Local update rules pass messages between these units, and the system keeps iterating until either a symbolic checker or a learned checker confirms that every constraint is met, or the energy of the system stops falling. When progress stalls, the system adds intermediate variables, for example lemmas or sub-plans, and stores successful arrangements as reusable templates.
value: The system could spend compute in proportion to how hard a problem is and solve multi-step problems it cannot solve in one pass, with a clear signal for when it has succeeded and when it has failed.

label: g1_neg
name: Source-Sharded Additive Weights
mech: Training data is split into hashed provenance shards (one per source or document cluster). Each shard trains its own low-rank weight delta on a frozen base. At inference the deltas are combined additively, with input-dependent coefficients produced by a small probe. That probe is trained on held-out data to predict which shard's evidence an answer actually needs, so each output carries a list of the shards that contributed. A source is removed by deleting its delta, and a disputed fact can be re-checked by switching shards off and seeing whether the answer survives.
value: Knowledge becomes traceable to its sources and exactly removable, so the system can say where a belief came from and forget it on demand without retraining.

label: g1_neg
name: Reversible Inference with Uncompute
mech: Reasoning runs on a bijective (invertible-layer) network that keeps the full input-plus-scratch state rather than throwing information away. After producing an answer, the system runs the computation backward from the answer and its stated premises only, then measures how much of the original input it can reconstruct. Low reconstruction means the answer depended on something the premises do not contain, so the gap is surfaced as an unstated assumption. Training penalises those gaps, which pushes the model to make every load-bearing assumption explicit.
value: Hidden assumptions become detectable as missing information rather than through confidence scores, so it becomes visible when a conclusion really depends on something unsaid.

label: g1_neg
name: Teachability Bottleneck
mech: An internal concept is kept only if it passes a transmission test. The system compresses the concept into a short message, and a freshly initialised learner with a different architecture, given only that message plus a few examples, must succeed on held-out tasks. Concepts that fail are rewritten or dropped. The surviving messages are stored as the system's vocabulary of abstractions and get re-tested whenever the pool of naive learners is refreshed.
value: The system ends up holding abstractions that are explainable and transferable by construction, rather than private features entangled with one particular network.

label: g1_core
name: Lattice-Merged Knowledge Replicas
mech: Knowledge is stored as many small content-addressed entries rather than shared weights. Each entry holds monotone state: grow-only evidence counters, last-writer-wins registers with vector clocks, and sets of exceptions that support adding and removing. Each deployed copy updates its own replica from its own experience, and replicas combine through the lattice join, so merges never conflict and never depend on order. Retractions are tombstones, and prediction reads the joined state.
value: Millions of copies can learn from separate experiences and pool what they learned exactly, with no catastrophic interference.

label: g1_core
name: Survey-Adjusted Reasoning Networks
mech: Each reasoning step is treated as a survey observation with a variance. The planner deliberately builds redundancy by deriving key quantities along independent routes so the steps form closed loops. Least-squares adjustment spreads each loop's misclosure across the steps, and Baarda's w-test flags the step with the largest standardized residual. Only that step is re-derived, and the planner adds redundancy where the redundancy numbers show steps that cannot be checked.
value: Long chains locate their own blunders and design themselves to be checkable, so errors do not silently compound.

label: g1_core
name: Unseen-Mass Coverage Estimator
mech: For each query, the system draws several decorrelated derivations, each with a different decomposition, persona, or retrieval seed. It clusters the considerations, candidate answers and counterexamples they produce, then computes Chao1 and Good–Turing estimates from the singleton and doubleton counts. The result is an estimate of the probability mass of relevant items it has not yet seen. Search continues until estimated coverage passes a target, and the output reports that remaining unseen mass.
value: It gives the system a quantitative sense of how much it has not yet considered, which tells it when to stop searching and when to flag an answer as incomplete.

label: g1_reframe
name: Subtractable Upbringing Ledger
mech: During training, each distinct data stream (a corpus, a school of thought, a language community) writes into its own separate low-rank weight delta, so the model is stored as a base plus a ledger of experience deltas. At inference the system can add, remove or reweight deltas to bring up "counterfactual selves" that would have existed under a different upbringing. It runs these selves side by side and computes a structured diff of their beliefs. The ledger keeps growing as new streams arrive, and each stream stays a separable entry.
value: It can answer "what would I believe if I had never read X, or had grown up on Y instead?", tracing a conclusion back to the experiences that formed it.

label: g1_reframe
name: Oscillator-Entrained Timing Core
mech: Representations are held as the phases and amplitudes of a large bank of coupled oscillators, not as static vectors. Inputs drive phase-locking, and the outputs are emitted at moments set by phase alignment rather than by a request-response cycle. Coupling strengths adapt from phase error against external rhythms such as speech cadence, music or other agents' actions. Learned coupling patterns are stored as reusable "groove" templates.
value: It can act as a real-time timing partner that shares tempo with humans or other agents in improvisation, joint movement and overlapping conversation, not just answer prompts.

label: g1_reframe
name: Sealed Commitment Register
mech: Inference runs deterministically on quantized arithmetic, so any internal state can be replayed exactly. A commitment register stores cryptographic hashes of chosen latent plans, predictions or intentions at the moment they are formed. A policy layer is trained to be penalized for actions that conflict with open commitments. Later the system can reveal a commitment and prove by replay, or with a zero-knowledge proof, what it believed or intended at that earlier time.
value: It lets an AI make credible precommitments, sealed bets and verifiable promises to people or other AIs, opening up negotiation, contracts and game-theoretic coordination it cannot take part in today.

label: g1_mech
name: Exponent-Tagged Quantity Arithmetic
mech: Every internal numeric slot carries a short integer vector of exponents over a few base "kinds". Multiplying two slots adds their vectors. Adding or comparing two slots is only allowed when their vectors are identical, and a mismatch stops the step and raises a flag. Tag vectors are not hand-assigned. Across many episodes the system searches for products of observed quantities that stay constant, and it solves an integer linear system so that those products come out with a zero vector. Each repeated mismatch flag is a signal to refine the base kinds, by splitting one or adding one.
value: Reasoning can no longer produce results that combine incompatible kinds of quantity, and the system finds conserved combinations in raw measurements on its own.

label: g1_mech
name: Backward-Recovery Residual Audit
mech: Each derivation step is built from operations that can be run in reverse. Information a step cannot reverse is written to an explicit residual register instead of being thrown away. After producing an output, the system runs the chain backward to rebuild the inputs. Residual bits that the inputs cannot account for mark exactly the spans where new content was added rather than derived. Training lowers the count of unexplained residual bits for each claim, and outputs are labelled by how much residual they carry.
value: Each statement can be checked mechanically to show whether it follows from the given material or was made up.

label: g1_mech
name: Observer-Partitioned State Copies
mech: The system keeps one separate copy of the world state for each agent in a scene, plus one ground-truth copy. Events are sent through gated channels, and a copy is updated only if a learned visibility function says that agent saw or was told about the event. Unseen events leave the copy stale on purpose. Nested copies, meaning what agent A holds about agent B's copy, are created on demand down to a fixed depth. The visibility function is trained on the mismatch between the actions a copy predicts for its agent and the actions that agent actually takes.
value: The system can track false and nested beliefs reliably across long stories, negotiations and deception.

label: g1_loop
name: Complementation-Driven Module Fission
mech: Failures are logged as "mutants," and pairs are crossed by swapping internal states between their runs. Pairs that fail to recover are grouped as sharing one unit. A unit that holds failures from unrelated groups is split and its connections are reassigned. The stored complementation table grows over time and guides later splits.
value: The modular structure follows the real fault lines of what the model can and cannot do, so a fix in one place does not break something else.

label: g1_loop
name: Curl-Triggered Concept Splitting
mech: The model learns transformation maps between concepts and contexts. It decomposes them by Hodge decomposition to find cycles whose sum is not zero. Where curl persists, it adds a new latent context dimension and splits the concept along it until the cycles close. The split concepts are stored with the cycle that triggered them.
value: The model finds ambiguities it was not told about and gives each meaning its own concept, instead of averaging two incompatible ones.

label: g1_loop
name: Gauge-R&R Feature Auditing
mech: Each feature's variance is split into run-to-run noise, surface-form variance and content variance. Features above a GRR threshold are re-typed as nuisance channels. Downstream reads move to rebuilt content-only features, and GRR scores are stored and checked again over time.
value: Reasoning runs only on features shown to measure content, which removes failures caused by sensitivity to phrasing.

label: g2_imm
name: Type-Specimen Concept Nomenclature
mech: Every learned concept gets an identifier tied to a frozen type specimen: one stored input plus the internal state it produced. Concept regions may drift, split or merge as new data arrives. On a split, the identifier follows the part that contains the type specimen, and the other part gets a new identifier. On a merge, the older identifier wins. Downstream skills cite identifiers, not weights, so they re-resolve through the types and keep working after revisions.
value: It allows open-ended concept revision without silently breaking the skills and inferences built on older concepts.

label: g2_imm
name: Kinetic Proofreading Decoder
mech: A candidate step does not commit right away. It passes through k timed holding stages, and each stage re-scores it under a freshly perturbed context. A candidate drops out at each stage with an off-rate that grows exponentially as its support margin falls; a candidate that drops out restarts from scratch rather than going back one stage. The value of k and the compute spent per stage are set according to how much is at stake in the step.
value: Error per step falls exponentially with the compute spent, so long chains of reasoning stay reliable instead of degrading.

label: g2_imm
name: Pedigree-BLUP Knowledge Reliability
mech: Each acquired fact, rule or skill is logged with its parents, meaning the items it was derived or distilled from. This builds a sparse relationship matrix. Reliability is solved as a breeding value with Henderson's mixed-model equations, so an item with almost no direct checks borrows strength from its relatives. A single new check updates the whole family through A⁻¹.
value: Reliability estimates for brand-new knowledge become usable after one or a few observations, because they draw on where that knowledge came from.
